newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares sit on early gains, yen hits dlr.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares sit on early gains, yen hits dlr.

text.p: European shares were ahead but off their best by midday on Friday after sprinting higher in early trade on the strength of another record close on Wall Street. Elsewhere, the dollar tried to steady against the yen after taking a battering on Thursday but only came under further pressure. European share traders drew early comfort from the U.S. Dow Jones industrial average which set its 19th record close of the year on Thursday, ending up 47.39 points at 7,333.55 -- its first close above 7,300 -- as it eclipsed Monday's record finish of 7,292.75.
Conflicting economic news has sent mixed signals on whether the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank will raise interest rates when its policy-making Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on Tuesday.

"We see a 50/50 chance that the Fed may raise rates just to continue with their pre-emptive strike but the inflation numbers have looked pretty good this week," said U.S. based analyst Elaine Garzarelli, who remains bullish with a year-end target of 7,600 for the Dow.

In bullion markets, gold opened firmer at $347.50 versus London's close of $346.95 and was then fixed at $347.00. The market was very quiet, having shrugged off German plans to revalue gold, but not sell any of its holdings.

London's FTSE 100 started the last session of a record-breaking week by moving up around 0.7 percent after Wall Street's strong finish. The index was 16 points or 0.3 percent higher at 4,697.2 by 1115 GMT.

The FTSE 100 came off its new record high after the index options expiry at 0930 GMT. It hit a fresh intra-day high of 4,723.7 immediately before the expiry amid position-closing ahead of the weekend and next Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy setting unit, FOMC.

"We're still squeezing up, there are bulls and bears and the picture is mixed but overall we are seeing people closing positions at the week end and some boys are getting caught short," said one senior dealer.
French stocks rose to all time highs, bolstered by gains in bond prices, Wall Street shares and a fresh Ipsos poll showing the conservatives leading in the upcoming parliamentary election.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.72 points, or 0.67 percent, at 2,794.73 at 0900 GMT.

An Ipsos poll for the magazine Le Point projected the ruling RPR-UDF coalition would win 323 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, up from 290 in a similar poll last week. It indicated the Socialists would trail with 266 seats.
Surveys by other polling institutes have shown even clearer leads for the centre-right in recent days.
German shares were around one percent higher, up 40.67 at 3,602.78, underpinned by Wall Street's close and the dollar's foray above 1.70 marks.

In currencies, the dollar traded slightly firmer against the mark and yen early in Europe as the markets stabilised following a volatile week of sharp yen gains and shifting interest rate expectations in Japan and the United States.
The rally soon faltered however and the U.S. currency stood at around 115.75 yen, well off its overnight high of 117.00 yen, and at 1.7025 marks at 1115 gmt.

Traders in Tokyo said the overnight session was dominated by a reaction to this week's steep decline in dollar/yen which was seen to be overdone. The recovery was limited and capped at 117 yen. Dollar/mark continued to outperform and held firm above 1.70 in Europe.
"Things are calmer and people seem to be digesting what was a very eventful week. We're starting to focus now on the FOMC next week," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.

"The big question now is whether the U.S. economy has slowed enough to prevent the Fed from tightening and on balance we think they will leave rates unchanged next week," said Knuthsen. "The market has scaled back its expectations and if they do raise rates the dollar could get a boost."
The dollar/yen has collapsed from 4-1/2-year highs this month and lost almost 10 percent of its value in just two weeks.

The reversal was triggered by a barrage of verbal intervention from Japanese officials aimed at preventing the yen weakening further and hastening the need for higher Japanese interest rates. Growing speculation about a rise Japanese rates, nevertheless, has reinforced the yen recovery, said analysts.
STOCK PRICES AT 1115 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 16.0 points at 4,697.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 19.84 points at 2,795.85.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 40.67 points at 3,602.78.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7025 marks and 115.78 yen compared with 1.6986 marks and 116.26 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $347.00 versus London's close of $346.95 on Thursday.
